get.description: Lists account_access grants across accounts. requester=me (default) returns the caller's own requests. requester=approvable returns other people's pending requests on accounts the caller may approve for. At most 200 rows, newest first. SystemAdmin only.

post.description: A Flume SystemAdmin asks to act inside one customer account (DEC-040). The account comes from the body; X-Flume-Account-ID is not read. The grant starts pending. A second person who is an approver for that account approves it and sets the expiry; the requester never approves their own grant. The grant does not gate entry: a SystemAdmin enters any account by role (FL-32223). While the grant is in force, requests that name the account with X-Flume-Account-ID (REST or MCP) or account_id (MCP) carry the grant on their scope, and each use is recorded before the request is served. SystemAdmin only.

Returns the "summary through message K" compaction checkpoint for a conversation, letting a resume skip the Haiku recompute (FL-30802). 404 when the conversation has no checkpoint — the client maps 404 to "no checkpoint" and resumes normally. The summary is customer conversation content and is read only from the account's own bucket-resident storage. account_id is derived from the request context, never sent by the client.

put.description: Writes (upserts) the compaction checkpoint for a conversation (FL-30802). The summary is customer conversation content and is written only to the account's own bucket-resident storage — never shared cross-customer storage. One checkpoint per conversation; a later write replaces the earlier one. 404 when the conversation does not belong to the caller, or when the account has no bucket-resident storage to hold it (the client treats 404 as "not persisted" and continues). account_id is derived from the request context, never sent by the client.

post.description: The holder hands the seat to the requester (handOver true) or keeps it (false; the request stays with the answer "kept") (FL-31670). 409 when the caller is not the holder or there is no open request.

Makes the caller the conversation's holder (FL-31452, spec-e9-projects.md "Concurrency, v1"). Succeeds when the lock is free or the existing hold has lapsed; 409 when someone else holds an unexpired claim. A holder re-claiming their own lock extends it — this is also how a client heartbeats to keep an active hold. The optional body {"activity": true} says the holder just sent or typed, which moves the seat's active time; a renewal without it does not. An empty body is the same as {"activity": false}.
Clears the caller's hold on the conversation, if it is currently theirs (FL-31452). 409 when it is not — already released, or expired and taken over by someone else.

Records the caller's request for a seat held by someone else (FL-31670). 409 when the seat is free or the caller's own, or when the holder kept the seat against this caller less than five minutes ago.

Reports present, missing and extra rows. Writes nothing. SystemAdmin only.

Mode "dry-run" (default) reports; mode "apply" writes only the MISSING rows, one per row, idempotently, and never revokes — extra rows are reported for a human. A 403 from context-db on apply is reported per account as applyRefused: it means the environment has not named the backend identity as context-db's grant provisioner. SystemAdmin only.

Reports whether the :Account anchor exists in the authenticated account's graph. Writes nothing. An account with a knowledge capability enabled and state "missing" is the alertable "flags on, anchor missing" condition — ambient knowledge retrieval returns nothing in that state while every other surface reports success.

post.description: Creates the :Account anchor in the authenticated account's graph if it is absent, and verifies it with a control read. Idempotent — an account that already has the anchor is read and not written. This is the repair path for an account whose flags were enabled before automatic provisioning existed, or whose provisioning failed.

502.description: context-db accepted the upsert but the anchor is not readable

get.description: Returns the whole account's scanned estate — every Server/Database/Schema/Table/View/StoredProcedure/Procedure/SSIS* vertex, with parent links, plus a Connection and Schema derived from each node's ancestry — in one response. Replaces the ~11 concurrent POST graph:query calls the schema tree used to fire per label (FL-31940, measured 2.6s cold / 1.6s warm on the largest account at the time, against a 2s target). The account comes from request context only. Honours If-None-Match with 304 against the ETag; the same ETag is returned as the ETag response header. truncated reports that the account has more estate nodes than one read covers — the client should treat the tree as partial, not retry.

304.description: the estate is unchanged since the If-None-Match etag

get.description: Runs every named check (storage, grants, dataset, anchor, flags, domains, indexes) against the authenticated account's knowledge graph and reports what each would do — present, created, repaired, or unsupported, with a reason. Writes nothing. A never-provisioned account typically reports grants as created (a POST would apply the backend identity's missing rows) and everything downstream — dataset, anchor, flags, indexes — as unsupported, blocked by grants: reads and writes against context-db need the same grants, so this action cannot check further until they exist. knowledge_staff_only is reported only while the account's capabilities are not yet live — once live, it drops out of the checked set entirely (its absence may be a deliberate release) and so out of the drift summary too. Includes a top-level drift summary (indexes always excluded — see the field's own doc). The domains check on GET is a dry run: it forecasts counts from the rules and from earlier model answers and calls no model. Also reports a counts-only knowledge census: entries per kind and status, ontology entries with and without children, and entries whose kind is outside the built-in set. An ontology entry with children is drift of type "section kind is ontology". SystemAdmin only.

409.description: a foreign vertex occupies the reserved anchor fqn

504.description: exceeded its budget; re-run, every check is idempotent

post.description: Runs every named check (storage, grants, dataset, anchor, flags, domains, indexes) and repairs what it can: creates an absent dataset and :Account anchor in one write, applies missing context-db grants, creates or fixes the knowledge flags flags selects, gives every Table vertex a data domain from names only (rules first, then the gateway model for tables the rules leave Unclassified) and reports per-table counts before and after, and re-indexes vertex ANN coverage. Idempotent for every check but indexes, which always reports repaired on a successful run (context-db carries no before/after coverage signal, so a call with nothing stale to fix reports the same as one that fixed something). An empty body is the SAFE default: on an account whose capabilities are not yet live it writes knowledge_staff_only before any capability flag, so a customer account never comes out open to its own users; on an account whose capabilities are already live it leaves knowledge_staff_only alone entirely, so an ordinary call can never re-restrict a customer account an operator deliberately released. Provisioning an empty account is not a special case: it is what this call does when every check starts absent. A check blocked by an earlier one (no storage bucket, grants not yet applied) reports unsupported and names the blocker rather than attempting a write context-db would refuse. account_id and accountId may NOT be set in the body; the account comes from request context only (X-Flume-Account-ID) and either spelling is rejected with 400. SystemAdmin only.

parameters.description: flags: default (safe, restricted), default-internal (no external users), or none; empty body means default
parameters.name: body

post.description: Mints or normalizes the estate FQN for each candidate (AD-12): repo://<host>/<org>/<repo> from a git remote, normalizing ssh/https shape, a trailing .git, and host case to one address per repository; ticket://<host>/<project>/<key> from a ticket key, resolved against the caller's account's configured Jira site. Writes nothing. A repo candidate reads no account data at all; a ticket candidate reads the caller's own account's configured Jira tenant hostname and reflects it into a resolved fqn. Every authenticated role may call it. A candidate whose kind this resolver does not yet implement, or a ticket key with no Jira site configured for the account, comes back state "unsupported"; a candidate that does not parse as its kind's shape (a git remote that matches none of the shapes git accepts, a key that is not PROJECT-NUMBER) comes back state "not_found". Neither is an error, and fqn is set if and only if state is "resolved" — this route never invents an address for a candidate it could not resolve. results is INDEX-ALIGNED with candidates: results[i] is always the outcome for candidates[i], and array position is the only supported way to correlate a result back to its candidate.

post.description: Returns the governed ambient knowledge index for a chat turn (FS-82): the anchor + semantic channels, scope-filtered and reciprocal-rank-fused, projected to compact pointers {id, title, hook, source_ref, score}. The account comes from request context only; account_id and accountId may NOT be set in the body — either spelling is rejected with 400. The anchor channel runs over the supplied anchors PLUS mentioned-entity anchors the server derives from the query — estate entities named in prose by the query string (FL-30820). The derivation reads query and nothing else; send an anchor for every entity you want anchored, because a paraphrased or embedding-optimized query derives fewer. At least one of query or anchors is required; top_k, when supplied, must be an integer between 1 and 1000 — the SAME request-shape validation the MCP graph-search index view enforces. This surface serves the INDEX view only (compact pointers, no bodies); view=full is rejected here with 400 because full corpus bodies are served by neither surface yet — MCP graph-search view=full runs the estate+knowledge search, a different gate and shape, not the governed index with bodies. Selection and scope governance are the resolver's. A knowledge-empty account, a restricted visitor, and an account with the read/inject capability off all return a byte-identical empty index (same body, headers, and status), and that empty index carries a stable constant etag — the same value for every account and every empty path — so an etag is ALWAYS present on a 200 and the empty case caches and 304s like any other. A shown-audit row is written only when the gateway stamped a turn identity onto the request; a non-gateway call writes none and says so via the X-Knowledge-Shown-Audit: not-recorded header. Honours If-None-Match with 304 against the etag; the etag is also returned as the ETag response header.

get.description: Lists curated knowledge for the authenticated account, each entity with a metadata-only summary of its linked artifacts (FL-30678), ordered by fqn and filterable by scope, kind, status, and fqn-prefix. The agent reads knowledge via graph-search/graph-query (K1); this is the CURATOR/manage surface. One curator-scoped rule applies: a NON-curator never sees status=proposed rows (unapproved content is what the review-queue and proposal-list gates protect, and an inventory must not route around them); a non-curator filtering for proposed gets an empty list, not an error. The result is BOUNDED (limit defaults to 200, ceiling 1000) and the envelope carries no cursor, so an account past the ceiling is truncated — the truncation is logged server-side, and wire pagination is the fix rather than a larger bound.

post.description: Creates a knowledge entity. account_id comes from request context, fqn is store-minted (C16), and curator_role from auth — none may be supplied in the body. TWO paths share this route by a body-value dispatch on status (AIP: not a bespoke verb): the default status=active is the CURATOR-gated create, while status=proposed is the save-this proposal (FL-29879) — NOT curator-gated, any authenticated author may propose. A proposal lands status=proposed plus one review_items row and is never retrieval-eligible until a curator approves it via the row-scoped review-items/{review_item_id}:approve. The propose-only evidence fields (proposed_target, sensitivity, verification_interval) are accepted ONLY with status=proposed; the source evidence link rides in source_refs, which already documents exactly that purpose.

Persists a content-addressed :Artifact (code/document/image). Identity is the content_hash (derived from the payload; a supplied hash is verified). Byte-identical content dedups to one row (FR-33). Raw PHI bytes are never injected — only the sanitized extracted_text is embedded/injected. A binary artifact's `bytes` are retained (FL-30227), stored against the content_hash outside the graph and served only through GET /api/v1/context/knowledge/artifacts/{content_hash}/content, which is role- and sensitivity-gated. Identity, size, media_type, extracted_text, and sensitivity/scope persist on the artifact itself.

delete.description: Erases a knowledge artifact. SystemAdmin-only, and deliberately NOT open to the account's own Admin, who curates the rest of this facade by role — so this is stricter than the rest of this facade's curator writes. It destroys the stored payload with no undo, and the payload read (GET .../content) already refuses an account Admin any artifact that is phi_bearing, unclassified, or scoped narrower than the account, because an :Artifact carries no scope_id to match a requester against; admitting that caller to the delete would let them destroy bytes they are refused a look at. WHAT THIS DELIVERS: the :Artifact row is marked erased and its content-bearing fields (source, extracted_text) are emptied, its revision edges are severed, and the stored payload is removed — after which every governed read answers not-found. TWO THINGS IT DOES NOT DELIVER, both stated in the response rather than implied away. The graph ROW is not removed: context-db has no vertex delete, so an erasure marks the row, and physical removal is a later sweep (FL-30445); `record_semantics` says so on every call. And the payload bytes are not reclaimed: Lance records a deletion vector rather than rewriting the fragment, so the bytes remain in the customer bucket and in older dataset versions until compaction and version cleanup run; `semantics` relays the storage layer's own sentence and bytes_reclaimed is always false. Refused with 409 while any knowledge entity still references the artifact, or while any later revision names it as a predecessor — unlink or retract those first. Deleting an artifact that does not exist is a 404; re-deleting one already erased is a 200 that records no second erasure and re-attempts whatever the first call left unfinished. One `erased` audit event is written, before anything is removed and only on the first erasure.

parameters.description: Artifact content hash (sha256- followed by 64 lowercase hex characters)
parameters.name: content_hash

409.description: still referenced, or has later revisions

500.description: partial delete — the message names which half survived and whether a re-run is required

get.description: Streams the raw bytes of a stored binary artifact, addressed by content_hash. Requires Editor or above; a phi_bearing or unclassified artifact additionally requires a curator (SystemAdmin). Returns 404 when no payload is stored — including for artifacts created before payload persistence existed, whose bytes were discarded and cannot be recovered except by re-creating the artifact from the same content. Raw bytes are never injected or embedded; only the sanitized extracted_text is.

Returns the knowledge graph around focus (a knowledge id) or, when focus is omitted, around the account root: sections and the entries filed under them (generated `path:` folders included, marked `generated`), every stored relationship between two entries the caller can see (SUPERSEDES, CONFLICTS_WITH, knowledge-to-knowledge APPLIES_TO), and each entry's APPLIES_TO attachment to an estate object as its own node (`node_type` estate, term, or account). Every node name resolves server-side, never a bare fqn. `depth` is how many levels below the focus unfold: for the root, 1 is the top-level sections, 2 adds what is filed directly under them; omitted or 0 means every level of the base under the focus; an explicit depth is capped at 5. A leaf focus returns its placement, its relationships in both directions, and its attachments. The response is capped at 500 nodes; a capped answer has `truncated: true`, `truncation_reason: node_cap`, and `total_nodes`. A base filed deeper than `depth` answers `truncated: true` with `truncation_reason: depth`, so `truncated: false` is the only reading of "this is everything under the focus". `truncation_reason` is one of four: `entity-ceiling` or `page-budget` when the corpus is larger than one scan can see, then `node_cap`, then `depth` — widest cut first. Gated and PHI-withheld exactly like the tree and the page read: an edge is drawn only between two nodes of the response, so a withheld or out-of-project entry is never named.

get.description: Returns one entry's in-place edits, newest first. Each edit names the changed fields and carries each field's value before and after the edit, the editor's display name (never an email or raw id) and the edit time. Gated like /base/page — an entry the page would not serve (absent, foreign, scope-unreadable, not active, or PHI-withheld) answers not_found — plus the curator gate, because a history holds content an edit removed. An erased entry's history is redacted with the entry. At most 200 edits are returned; truncated reports that older edits were left out.

Gated like the tree, the page and the graph: every account user who can engage with knowledge may read it. Two fields the SPA has asked for are not on this response because no reliable source exists yet: per-entry recent activity (no audit-log read exists by account or by fqn) and a 30-day usage count (the injection-audit read is turn-addressed, not account-scoped) — see the PR that added this route.

Gated and PHI-withheld exactly like the tree and the markdown export: a phi_bearing/phi_adjacent entry, or one linking an unclassified/missing artifact, answers not_found — never a 403 that would confirm the fqn exists.

get.description: Lists status=proposed knowledge items awaiting curator review (FR-7, FR-27). Account-isolated and CURATOR-GATED (a non-curator gets 403, even though the route-level policy admits editors) — the list carries unapproved proposal content. Each entry is hydrated from the LIVE :Knowledge node, so a curator's edits before approval are what the queue shows; the reason comes from the review row.

get.description: Returns everything the propose->active promotion gate needs, in one read (FL-29879's 2026-08-05 AC): the proposal's §3.4 evidence, the FR-27 field NAMES it is missing, and a FRESH artifact-revision verdict. Both gate results are server-authoritative — missing_evidence because several FR-27 fields are not on ProposalPayload at all, and artifact_freshness because the revision flip skips proposed referrers, so the proposal's own needs_review badge reads clean on exactly the case this catches. It writes nothing and is safe (and intended) to re-run on every promotion-dialog open: a verdict computed at mount would answer with the graph as it was at mount, and the failure this exists for is a revision landing while the proposal waited. CURATOR-gated. A row that is not a proposed_knowledge item has no promotion to preflight (400).

post.description: Disposes a review row as accepted. On a proposed_knowledge row this is ONE call that does BOTH halves of the promotion: it promotes the entity proposed->active (emitting the `approved` event) and disposes the row open->accepted. They are one call because the two writes span different datasets with no shared transaction, so the sequencing has to be the server's — a client issuing two calls would own a half-applied promotion it cannot repair. On a bulk_seed_ambiguity or feedback_flag row there is no entity to promote, so it is queue bookkeeping only. Promotion enforces the FR-27 evidence floor AND the artifact-freshness re-check, refusing with 400 invalid_input and a `field` naming what blocked it (`artifacts` for a revised or unconfirmable artifact, `section_fqn` for a non-section entry, otherwise the missing evidence field) — a `section_fqn` naming NO entry at all refuses 404 not_found instead, the same split `:place` draws. A refused promotion writes NOTHING. Knowledge-hierarchy placement (FL-31444, D37): an entry that ends up filed nowhere — no `section_fqn` override, no inherited or resolved target, no curator pre-approval filing — lands in Unfiled under the account root, and the response's `placement` field says so ("Placed in Unfiled"); it is empty when the entry resolved a real placement of its own. CURATOR-gated.

post.description: Disposes a review row as dismissed — the curator judged it not actionable. PURE queue bookkeeping on every item type: no knowledge effect and no knowledge_audit_log event, because a queue transition is not itself a :Knowledge state change (§1.5 keeps the two logs distinct). This is the feedback_flag disposition; a triage prompt is not a proposal, so it is never "rejected". CURATOR-gated.

Folds a proposed_knowledge row's content into an EXISTING entity and disposes the row as accepted. There is deliberately no `merged` audit event — the sixteen-type set is closed, and a merge decomposes into exactly two recorded effects: an `edited` event on the target and an `approved` event on the review item. Only the target is client-supplied; the FIELDS folded are derived server-side from the proposal (from the LIVE node, so a curator's pre-merge edits are what lands), because letting a client name them would make merge a general edit wearing a proposal's disposition. Only a proposed_knowledge row can be merged. CURATOR-gated.
post.summary: Merge a proposal into an existing entity

post.description: Disposes a review row as rejected. On a proposed_knowledge row it also terminates the entity (proposed->rejected) and emits a `rejected` event carrying the reason when one is supplied; the body is optional, because a curator dispositioning without typing a reason sends none. Rejecting a knowledge entity that is not a proposal is a 409 — `rejected` is a proposal-lifecycle terminus, not a general retraction (that is DELETE/tombstone). CURATOR-gated.

get.description: Without the target_fqn parameter, returns what has been shared WITH the calling user — the "shared with me" inbox. With it, returns who that one artifact has been shared with, which is what the artifact row's "Shared with" line renders. The parameter is read by PRESENCE: supplying it blank is a 400, not a request for the inbox. Both arms are scoped to the caller's account. Both are capped at the 200 most recent rows and the response carries no cursor, so a client must not present a full-length list as complete.

parameters.name: target_fqn

post.description: Points another user of the SAME account, identified by email, at an artifact — a generated deck, dashboard, document or query, addressed as artifact/{content_hash}. This is a handoff record, not an access grant: it records who pointed whom at what, and confers no read. The recipient opens the artifact through the governed payload route and its unchanged gate, so a recipient who may not see a phi_bearing, unclassified or narrowly-scoped artifact still cannot, and receives that route's refusal. A recipient who is not a user on the caller's account is refused with 404. A knowledge fqn is refused with 400 — share the artifact, not the claim. Re-sharing the same artifact to the same person returns the existing record rather than failing.
post.summary: Share an artifact with a teammate

get.description: Returns the injected-knowledge panel + RecallTrace payload for a conversation turn (FR-24). A zero-injection turn returns gate_decision=none with no recall_trace. SOURCE: an in-process retention ring serves the hot path, and a ring miss READS THROUGH to the durable injection_audit table in the account's own bucket (FL-30430), so a turn any replica served is answerable from any replica. That read-through is what makes the empty payload meaningful: gate_decision=none means the turn was not recorded as injecting anything, rather than 'the pod that served it is not this one' — BUT ONLY WHEN evidence='not_recorded', see below. A turn that was never recorded still returns the zero-injection payload, and this endpoint still never 404s for a missing turn. READ `evidence` BEFORE READING ANYTHING ELSE (FL-30627): it says whether this payload is an account of the turn at all. 'recorded' — a record was found and the payload describes it. 'not_recorded' — every source was consulted, none holds it, AND a source could have held it, and ONLY under this value does an empty injected set mean the turn injected nothing. SINCE FL-30795 NO DEPLOYED BUILD RETURNS IT: retiring the gateway {knowledge} token left the injection-audit trail with no production writer, so a genuine miss reports 'unavailable' instead and the workspace's own client-side injection is not visible to this route at all. It returns to service with FL-30841. Treat it as a value to handle, not one to expect. 'unavailable' — the record could not be looked for (no durable trail is wired on this instance, or its query endpoint has not deployed), so gate_decision=none and injected=[] are filler that keep the payload well-formed and assert NOTHING; clients MUST render this as 'couldn't load', exactly as they render a 503, and never as 'no knowledge applied'. This is the SECOND way this endpoint says 'couldn't load' and it arrives as a 200, because failing every read through a deploy-skew window would be worse than degrading. IT CAN ALSO RETURN 503: when the durable read itself fails (timeout, or the account's injection_audit is unreadable) the endpoint refuses rather than answering empty, because an outage and a turn that injected nothing are opposite claims — clients MUST render 503 as 'couldn't load', never as 'no knowledge applied'. An id that is not in the minted-id alphabet is refused with 400 before any lookup — that is a malformed request, not an outage, and retrying it will never succeed. ADDRESSING: the gateway mints a per-turn message id and returns it as the X-Flume-Message-Id response header on the LLM proxy call that served the turn (FL-30412) — read it there and address this route with it. A conversation id is also accepted, for clients that do not read that header yet, and resolves to that conversation's MOST RECENT retained turn — correct for a dock rendering the live answer, wrong for one pinned to an older answer. PER-ITEM FIDELITY: title, kind and scope are re-read from the entity at request time, so they reflect the entity NOW rather than at turn time; badge.freshness, conflict and phi are computed during retrieval and are NOT carried by the audit record, so they are absent/false here rather than recomputed from a second, divergable opinion.
get.summary: Get injected knowledge for a turn

parameters.description: Message id segment of the turn — the opaque id only, not a slash-bearing resource name (chi path params cannot contain a slash). Take it from the X-Flume-Message-Id response header of the LLM proxy call that served the turn. A conversation id is also accepted and resolves to that conversation's most recent retained turn.
parameters.name: message_id

get.description: Serves the SPA's runtime knowledge-UI state: a server-computed answer, not a projection of flag rows. can_curate reports whether THIS CALLER passes the curator gate — a Flume system admin, or the account's own Admin, by role — and is computed from the same predicate that refuses curator writes, so the UI cannot offer an action the API then refuses. It is a hint for rendering, never a permission: every write is gated server-side regardless. Always-on with respect to the capability flags, so it still answers under a rollback — the posture it most needs to answer in. FL-31440 retired the SPA UI kill-switch flag this route used to also report.

Curator-gated in the manager. Only an `active` entity can be archived; any other status answers 409. An entity with no attachments archives normally. Resolves target_text and enforces hard-required human-in-the-loop disambiguation (FR-4): 0 candidates offers :BusinessTerm creation (create_target_term to confirm), 1 auto-attaches, 2+ returns 409 disambiguate_required with candidates. A same-kind/same-target active returns 200 with a conflict_warning (not an error); resend with proceed=true to attach and record :CONFLICTS_WITH. post.description: Removes the :APPLIES_TO edge from this entity to target_fqn, the inverse of :attach. Edges only — the target node (an estate column, a business term, the account anchor) is never touched. Detaching an attachment that does not exist is a 404, never a silent 204: a delete of an absent edge is not an error in storage, so the route distinguishes it explicitly. Idempotent in effect but not in status — a second detach of the same target answers 404. A `detached` audit event is written whenever this call answers 204, and none is written on the 404 path; the event records that the attachment is gone, not that this particular call is what removed it — two curators racing the same target can each get a 204 and each write one. `target_fqn` is required and must not be blank: severing every attachment at once is archive, not detach.

post.description: Right-to-erasure. Empties every content-bearing surface on the entity — title, description, body, applicability, tags, source refs and the curator-typed attribution fields — regenerates the node vector from those emptied values, retires the entity so no retrieval channel returns it, and appends a terminal `erased` event to the append-only audit log as a redacted tombstone. Distinct from delete/tombstone, which redact the body only and keep the prose surfaces. Two things it does NOT do, both reported in the response rather than implied: the ROW is not removed (context-db exposes no vertex-delete, so a content-free shell keyed by the opaque id remains), and the BYTES are not gone when this returns (storage is copy-on-write, so the pre-erasure version persists until a maintenance sweep compacts it out and prunes the versions that referenced it, and a background sweep can do that only once the old version ages past retention and any object lock on the bucket, so there is no timeline to quote). See docs/knowledge-erasure-semantics.md for the byte timeline per bucket class.

post.description: Creates a new version, links :SUPERSEDES, and flips the prior version's temporal bounds. A genuine non-CRUD action (multi-node + side effects), so a colon custom method, not a field PATCH. A payload carrying status=proposed (FL-31264) instead lands as a DRAFT — not curator-gated, matching plain create — the predecessor is held on a review row and the link + flip run inside its later review-items/{id}:approve, in one act. Otherwise the precondition check, the successor mint, and the link + flip all run inside one atomic manager call. An if_updated_at that no longer matches the target's stored updated_at fails closed with 409 supersede_precondition_failed naming the current tip, before anything is created.

post.description: Bulk/seed/migration write. Never a per-item live stop (§2.1b): an item with an explicit target_fqn creates a knowledge node and attaches it to that target, which must already exist as an estate or business-concept node; an item carrying only target_text is written to review_items (a bulk_seed_ambiguity row — pointer+hash, never the raw body) and the batch proceeds, because this path runs no target resolver; input-shape failures and rejected targets are returned per item. No item may supply fqn, id, or account_id — identity is store-minted and the account comes from the request context. The manifest must carry between 1 and 500 items. Curator-gated. With dry_run the same admission rules run (shape checks and the target check, which is a read) without writing anything, so a preview never reports written for an item the real run would reject on its input — it cannot predict a store-level failure, which only the real write can hit. Each `deferred` entry is a PREVIEW of the row that would be created: item_type, status, reason, account_id and proposed_payload are exact, while review_item_id, source_event_id and created_at are minted at persist time. On a preview the two ids are OMITTED from the response; created_at is the one field that still carries a zero value ("0001-01-01T00:00:00Z") and must be treated as absent rather than parsed as a date.

Compacts and prunes every Lance dataset under the requesting account's graph warehouse, forcing materialization of every deletion, so the bytes behind erased knowledge entities leave storage. This is the second half of `:erase`, which cannot do it: storage is copy-on-write, so writing over a row does not unwrite the bytes it replaced. Also sweeps the knowledge datasets in the customer storage root (review queue, audit logs), where an erased entry's redacted review row leaves superseded bytes. Erasure completes across AT LEAST TWO sweeps rather than one call — a sweep cannot prune the versions it just wrote, so a `bytes_removed` of 0 is a normal result and a later run reclaims once the pre-erasure versions age past the retention window. If context-db refuses the sweep for a missing MAINTAIN grant, the response is 200 with `complete: false` and a detail naming POST /api/v1/context/grants:reconcile. SystemAdmin-only in the manager, and deliberately NOT open to the account's own Admin, who curates the corpus by role: the sweep rewrites the whole warehouse and destroys bytes, which is authority over the substrate rather than over the corpus. A 409 has two causes, and only one of them is overridable: context-db deferred because a scan is writing the same datasets (retry later, not a failure — an operator on a deadline can re-run with `{"quiesce_secs": 0}` to sweep anyway), or a sweep is already running for this account on this API instance (wait for it; `quiesce_secs` cannot clear this one, because the sweep survives the request that started it and stacking retries is what the guard prevents). That in-flight guard is per-instance, not per-deployment. The body is optional and `quiesce_secs` is the only field on it; nothing a request sends can weaken what the sweep does. See docs/knowledge-erasure-semantics.md.

parameters.description: Optional sweep options; an empty body uses the server defaults

Entries governed as PHI are withheld and counted in the X-Knowledge-Wiki-Withheld header and the manifest. `include` widens the default active-only export with `superseded` and/or `archived`. A missing or unknown `format` is a 400 that names the accepted values; an empty corpus on `format=markdown` is a 400 failed_precondition.

Curator-only. Entries governed as PHI are withheld and counted in the X-Knowledge-Wiki-Withheld header. `include` widens the default active-only export with `superseded` and/or `archived`.

post.description: Folds appended and rewritten fragments back into the graph datasets' indices. Does NOT compact and does NOT prune: it adds, changes, deletes and relocates no row, alters no schema, and moves nothing outside the account's own bucket, which is why it is exposed where the erasure sweep's irreversible steps are not. Use it when a warehouse's index has fallen behind its data — the state every compact-only sweep produced before FL-30982, because context-db compacts with remap_options None and rewritten fragments drop out of index coverage unless the same sweep re-optimizes. Takes no body. Returns context-db's maintenance report. 409 when context-db defers because a scan is actively writing the datasets; retry once ingest is quiet.

Creates the account's knowledge root and its system Unfiled section if either is absent, restores either one that exists but has drifted to a non-active or non-ontology state (`singletons_repaired`), files Unfiled under the root, and attaches a :PART_OF edge (the root for a section, Unfiled for anything else) to every ACTIVE existing node this scan finds with no :PART_OF edge at all (FL-31444). Idempotent: a second run against an already-reconciled account creates and places nothing. Draft, rejected, tombstoned, archived, and superseded nodes are never swept. The node scan is bounded: when an account has more knowledge vertices than one pass can read, the report returns `truncated: true` and the unscanned tail keeps no :PART_OF edge — re-running does not reach it, because the scan takes no cursor. SystemAdmin only — the same account-wide maintenance gate the erasure sweep uses, not the ordinary curator grant.

post.description: Applies a plan: creates its new areas, then files each entry under its area with the same single-parent move :place makes. A new area whose title matches an active area is reused, so a retry does not create a second copy. The whole plan is validated first and refused on a shape error; after that a failure on one area or entry is reported in errors and the rest of the plan still runs. At most 200 assignments and 40 new areas per call. With dry_run the plan is validated and counted and nothing is written. Curator-gated.

Reads the entries filed under Unfiled (or directly under from_section_fqn) and asks the assistant for a plan: new areas to create and one area per entry. Writes nothing. The plan is a draft: lines that name an entry or area that does not exist are dropped and counted, and entries the plan leaves out are listed as unassigned. At most 200 entries are covered per call; remaining says how many were left. Curator-gated.

Saves an answer from chat to the account's knowledge, filed under an area. The caller does not choose the outcome: the manager decides from the caller's role. An Admin's save publishes (outcome=publish). An Editor's save becomes a proposal an Admin approves (outcome=propose). A Viewer is refused (403). area_fqn must be an active area the caller can read; otherwise the save is refused and nothing is written. The body has no status, proposed_target or supersedes_fqn field, and an unknown field is refused.

post.description: Sets whether knowledge changes need review (FL-32297). review_required (the default): Admins publish, and Editors' changes become proposals an Admin approves. writers_publish: Admins and Editors publish directly. Viewers cannot change knowledge in either mode. Admins only. Every change is recorded in the account's graph with who, when, from and to. It takes effect on the next write.
post.summary: Set the account's knowledge publishing policy

auto.description: Auto is the classifier's own answer, kept whatever the override says.

after.description:
After counts tables by the domain they hold once the backfill is done. On a
dry run it is a forecast from the rules and from earlier model answers; it
makes no model call.

before.description: Before counts tables by the domain stored now. Tables with none count as "(unset)".

changed.description: Changed is how many tables need a write.

modelAnswered.description: ModelAnswered is how many of those the model gave a domain. Zero on a dry run.

needsModel.description:
NeedsModel is how many tables the rules could not classify and no override
or earlier model answer covers. On a dry run they are forecast Unclassified.
It is always zero when no model fallback is wired: no run can change those
tables, so counting them would report drift that nothing can clear.

tables.description: Tables is how many Table vertices the account's graph holds.

unclassifiedShare.description: UnclassifiedShare is After's Unclassified count over Tables, 0 to 1.

written.description: Written is how many tables this call wrote. It is zero on a dry run.

legacyScopeEntries.description: LegacyScopeEntries counts vertices whose stored scope is `project`.

legacyWorkspaces.description: LegacyWorkspaces counts workspaces with at least one such tuple.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the scope walk hit its page budget. The scope
count is then a lower bound.

counts.description: Counts is set only when the request asks for it with includeCounts=true.

confidence.description:
Confidence is the approver's own confidence score (FL-31944), greater than 0
and at most 1, for a proposal saved without one. Without it such a proposal
could never be approved, because no route edits a proposed entity.

proposed_target.description:
ProposedTarget is the attachment target the approver RESOLVED, and it is
another of those four fields (FL-30478).

The save-this dialog labels its own target field "a suggestion — the curator
resolves it before approving". Until this field existed the curator had no way
to do that here: proposed_target is required evidence, the approve body could
not carry one, so a proposal saved without a target was unapprovable and the
approve dialog offered no input to fix it. Supplying one here satisfies the
floor and is persisted on the promoted entity.

It attaches nothing — attach is a separate curator-gated custom method with its
own disambiguation and conflict detection. This is the same free-text field
propose accepts, supplied by a different actor at a later moment.

recall_policy.description: RecallPolicy overrides the auto-injection policy the entity goes live under.

section_fqn.description:
SectionFQN is the approver's EXPLICIT section placement (FL-31444, D37)
— distinct from ProposedTarget above, which is permissive free text
that degrades silently to Unfiled when it does not resolve. SectionFQN
must name an existing, active, ontology-kind knowledge entry (the same
rule `:place` enforces): a fqn naming NO node at all refuses the whole
approve not_found (404); one that resolves but is the wrong kind or
not currently active refuses invalid_input (400) naming the field —
"approve refuses only a placement that names a missing section."
Optional; when omitted, approval resolves placement the way it always
has and falls back to Unfiled only if that leaves the entry filed
nowhere — see the response's `placement` field.

sensitivity.description:
Sensitivity is the approver's own PHI classification (FL-31438), for a
proposal that carries none and whose predecessor (if a supersede draft)
carries none either. Until this field existed, an unclassified proposal
with an unclassified predecessor was permanently unapprovable — FR-27's
floor requires a known class and neither the draft nor the inheritance
rung had one to offer, with no approve-time input to fix it short of
editing the entity on the manage surface first.

source_refs.description:
SourceRefs is the approver's own evidence links (FL-31438), for a
proposal that carries none and whose predecessor carries none either —
the same gap as Sensitivity above, for FR-27's source-evidence-link
requirement.

verification_interval.description:
VerificationInterval overrides the re-verification cadence — an ISO-8601 duration
string such as "P90D", NOT a nanosecond count (see knowledgestore.Duration). It is
one of the four FR-27 fields an approver can supply for a proposal that carries
none, which is what keeps a promotion completable without a manage-surface round
trip.

edited_by.description:
EditedBy is the editor's resolved DISPLAY NAME (FL-31650), never an email or a
raw id; omitted when unresolved.

confidence.description:
Confidence and sensitivity are the entry's stored values, so an editor
opens on them rather than on a default (FL-31719).

created_by.description:
CreatedBy/VerifiedBy are resolved DISPLAY NAMES (FL-31650) — never an
email or a raw id — omitted when unresolved (no resolver wired, no
matching user, or the entity never records an actor for that axis).

links.description:
Links is every inline [[slug--shortid|Title]] reference Body carries,
resolved server-side (FL-31650).

section_fqns.description:
section_fqns and section_titles are index-parallel and report the entry's
EFFECTIVE filing — the same ranking /base/tree applies, so the breadcrumb here
never contradicts the tree. A generated `path:`-tag section has no page of its
own, so its section_fqns slot is "" and only its title is meaningful; that is
the same "no fqn means generated" convention BaseNode carries in the tree.

section_members.description:
SectionMembers is set only when this page is a section: its direct
entries and direct sub-sections (FL-31650). Absent for an ordinary
entry, and absent (best-effort) if the extra corpus scan failed.

verification_interval.description:
VerificationInterval is the entity's own raw "P{n}D" cadence, omitted
when unset.

bytes.description:
Bytes is the raw binary payload for a document/image artifact. Go's
encoding/json marshals a []byte as a base64 JSON string, so the wire
representation is base64; the swaggertype and format tags below record that
in the generated spec and client, which would otherwise model a []byte as an
array of integers.

bytes_reclaimed.description:
BytesReclaimed is false on every path today. Lance records a deletion vector
rather than rewriting the fragment, so the bytes remain in storage and in older
dataset versions until compaction and version cleanup run.

record_semantics.description:
RecordSemantics states what happened to the :Artifact ROW. It says the row
survives, because it does: context-db has no vertex delete, so an erasure marks
the row and empties its content-bearing fields rather than removing it, and every
governed read then answers not-found. Populated on every success — including the
re-delete of an already-erased artifact, which says so explicitly rather than
letting a caller read a second success as a second erasure.

semantics.description:
Semantics is the storage layer's plain-language statement of the PAYLOAD
guarantee. It is populated on every success, including the paths with no
substrate operation to describe: an artifact with no stored payload (a code
artifact, one created before payloads were persisted, or the second half of a
retry) gets an explicit sentence saying so. omitempty is kept for the zero value,
but no success path produces one — a response carrying no guarantee is the
reading this field exists to prevent.

bytes_reclaimed.description:
BytesReclaimed reports whether the pre-erasure bytes have left storage. Always
false on this response: storage is copy-on-write, so the bytes remain in storage
and in older dataset versions until compaction and version cleanup run. That is
the erasure sweep, which runs in the background and behind `:erasure-sweep`, and
it can reclaim them only once they age past version retention and any object
lock on the bucket, so there is no timeline to quote here.

content_redacted.description:
ContentRedacted reports that every content-bearing surface on the entity is
empty — title, description, body, applicability, tags, source refs and the
curator-typed attribution fields — and that the node vector was regenerated
from those emptied values.

detail.description:
Detail states the same thing in one sentence, for a surface that shows the
operator a message rather than reading the booleans.

retrievable.description:
Retrievable reports whether the entity can still reach a retrieval channel.
False once erased: the row is retired to a status every retrieval path filters.

row_removed.description:
RowRemoved reports whether the row itself left the graph. False today: what
remains is a content-free shell keyed by the opaque store-minted id.

status.description:
Status is always "erased" — the request succeeded. What that word covers is
the rest of this object, not this field.

quiesce_secs.description:
QuiesceSecs overrides context-db's ingest-quiesce window for this sweep. While
any dataset under the account's warehouse has a commit newer than the window,
context-db defers the sweep with 409 rather than race a live scan. Omit it to
use the server's window; send 0 to disable the gate for this request, which is
the override for an erasure that must run against a deadline instead of waiting
for ingest to go quiet. It is the answer to the 409, so it is deliberately
reachable by the same curator the 409 is returned to.

complete.description:
Complete is true only when every discovered dataset was swept. It is NOT a
statement that the erasure is complete, and it is the one field on this
response that can be read as one — which is why Detail below exists. A
partial sweep does not discharge an erasure obligation (the datasets that
failed may still hold the bytes the sweep was run to remove, and there is no
way from the report to tell which); a COMPLETE sweep does not necessarily
discharge it either, because a sweep cannot prune the versions it just wrote.

datasets_total.description:
DatasetsTotal is how many Lance datasets under the account's warehouse were
attempted — every one of them, not only the vertex table.

detail.description:
Detail says in one sentence what the fields above do and do not mean, for a
surface that shows the operator a message rather than reading them. Same
reasoning as EraseResponse.Detail, and this is the harder of the two responses
to read correctly.

failed_datasets.description:
FailedDatasets names the datasets that could not be swept. context-db withholds
the underlying error from its response on purpose (a rendered storage error can
embed object paths); the reason is in context-db's logs.

versions_removed.description:
VersionsRemoved / BytesRemoved / DataFilesRemoved are the reclamation actually
achieved by this run. Zero is a legitimate answer and usually the right one:
a sweep cannot prune the versions it just wrote, so bytes come back on later
runs as the pre-erasure versions age past the retention window.

body_truncated.description:
BodyTruncated reports that the model was handed only PART of this entity's
curated body: it exceeded the per-entity allowance and was cut to fit.
TRI-STATE like Conflict and PHI above — absent means nothing established it,
never "read in full".

conflict.description:
Conflict and PHI are TRI-STATE: true, false, or null for "not established".

They were plain booleans, which meant every row this API served asserted a definite
negative — including for entities whose governance nothing had read. For `phi` that
is the unsafe direction of an unsafe field: a curator opening the dock to judge
whether something should have reached a model was told "no PHI" about an entity
nobody classified. The rule is that unknown stays unknown; the same reasoning
reviewmanager's ToolCall.ResultEmpty documents for its own tri-state, and the same
distinction §3.1 already draws by OMITTING recall_trace rather than sending it empty.

omitempty, so unknown is ABSENCE rather than an explicit null. Two reasons, and the
first is decisive: swag renders a *bool as a plain `boolean`, so a null on the wire
would contradict the generated contract the SPA builds its types from (A5) — the
field would be typed `boolean` and arrive null. Absence is expressible in that
contract; null is not.

It is also unambiguous, which an earlier version of this comment got wrong: the
previous shape was a plain bool with no omitempty, so an older server ALWAYS sent
the key. An absent phi therefore cannot be version skew — it can only be this
server saying "not established".

description.example: Rows written before 2021-03 have a null paid_amt.

title.example: paid_amt is null before the 2021 migration

content.description: Content is the rendered block text ({ontology} or {index}).

version.description: Version is the block's monotonic version (ontology_version / account_index_version).

complete.description:
Complete is true only when every discovered dataset was re-indexed. Unlike the
erasure sweep's field of the same name, a false here has no compliance meaning
— it is a latency statement.

datasets_total.description:
DatasetsTotal is how many Lance datasets under the account's warehouse were
attempted.

detail.description: Detail spells out what Complete implies, so the field cannot be read alone.

duration_ms.description:
DurationMs is context-db's own measure of the run. On a badly-lagged warehouse
this is the number worth capturing — it is what says whether the operation fits
inside context-db's 300s ceiling on this estate.

failed_datasets.description:
FailedDatasets names the datasets that could not be re-indexed. Those keep
scanning until a later run succeeds.

exportable.description:
Exportable is false to keep an area, and everything filed under it, out of
export (FL-31877). It is valid on an area only.

current_content_hash.description:
CurrentContentHash names the head that replaced this version; absent when the
version IS the head. On a forked revision history it names ONE of several heads
(content-addressing lets a version have multiple successors, so there is no unique
"latest") — `revised` is the field that carries the verdict.

target_fqn.description: TargetFQN addresses the artifact being shared: `artifact/{content_hash}`.

evidence.description:
Evidence qualifies EVERY field below it, and is not omitempty on purpose: an
absent qualifier is how the unqualified payload got shipped in the first place.
See KnowledgeEvidence — only "recorded" and "not_recorded" license reading the
injected set as what the turn did.

recall_trace.description: RecallTrace is the at-a-glance banner list; ABSENT on a zero-injection turn.

suppressed.description:
C14 branch A — the suppressed set enumerated inline. Mutually exclusive with
SuppressedRef; a builder picks a branch by measurement.

suppressed_detail_ref.description:
C14 branch B — a handle the dock fetches on expand when inlining the full
suppressed set is too heavy for the turn payload.

can_curate.description:
CanCurate reports whether this caller passes the curator gate
(authz.KnowledgeCurate): a Flume system admin, or the account's own Admin. It is
what the SPA gates its curation surfaces on INSTEAD of the client-side
isSystemAdmin check, which would keep an account's own Admins looking at a
read-only UI.

SERVER-COMPUTED FROM THE SAME PREDICATE THAT REFUSES WRITES, deliberately.
It is knowledgemanager.CanCurate, defined as RequireCurator returning nil, so
the answer the client renders and the answer the write path enforces cannot
disagree. Recomputing the role-and-flag rules here — or in the client — would
make a UI that offers a button the API then refuses, or hides one it would
have allowed, the first time either side changed.

It is a HINT, not a permission. Nothing trusts the client to honor it: every
curator write is gated in the manager regardless of what this said.

A restricted account's own user gets the SAME computed answer as anyone
else (FL-31440): the write path admits an Admin on a staff-only account, so
the zero value would tell them they cannot curate when they can. See the
handler for why serving the real answer discloses nothing.

knowledge_publishing.description:
KnowledgePublishing is the account's knowledge publishing policy (FL-32297):
review_required or writers_publish. Omitted when the policy could not be read.

write_decision.description:
WriteDecision is what happens to this caller's knowledge change on this
account: publish (it goes live) or propose (an Admin reviews it). It is
knowledgemanager.DecideKnowledgeWrite, the same function the write path
applies, so the sentence the SPA shows ("Your changes publish immediately" or
"Your changes go to an Admin for review") cannot disagree with what a write
does. Omitted when the caller may not write knowledge or the decision could
not be made.

confidence.description:
Confidence is the optional [0,1] score for the attachment. Omit it to leave
confidence unset; a supplied value (including 0) is persisted distinctly from
unset, so "zero confidence" and "no confidence" do not collapse.

create_target_term.description:
CreateTargetTerm is the zero-candidate confirm step: when a target text
resolves to no candidate, the curator may confirm creating a :BusinessTerm to
attach to. When set, the manager mints the term and attaches the source to it in
one call (the offer→confirm flow), emitting the business-term-fallback metric.

proceed.description:
Proceed acknowledges a same-kind/same-target conflict warning: the first
interactive attach returns the warning and writes nothing; a follow-up with
Proceed=true writes the :APPLIES_TO edge AND records the :CONFLICTS_WITH edge
(FR-5). It has no effect when no conflict exists.

The two-call confirm is STATELESS, so Proceed is a blanket acknowledgment of
WHATEVER CONFLICTS EXIST AT PROCEED TIME, not of the specific conflicts a prior
call surfaced: a first call with Proceed=true skips the warning entirely, and a
conflict created between the warn and the proceed is written past without ever
having been shown. Accepted deliberately — FR-5's mechanical invariants still
hold either way (every conflict is detected, recorded as :CONFLICTS_WITH with an
`attached` audit event, and echoed in the result), so nothing is absorbed
silently; only the ORDER of "shown" versus "written" differs. If multi-curator
concurrency arrives, replace this with acknowledged-fqn semantics (e.g.
proceed_past: [existing_fqns]) rather than widening the blanket flag.

additional_conflicts.description:
AdditionalConflicts carries the second-and-later conflicts when multiple
explicit targets each hit a same-kind active (FR-5: every conflict is
surfaced, none silently absorbed). Additive so existing consumers of the
singular field keep working; empty when at most one conflict exists.

part_of_edges.description:
PartOfEdges are the :PART_OF edges this attach wrote — present when one or more
target_fqns named an `ontology`-kind knowledge entry (FL-31304). A section
target never appears in Edges above: it is filed, not applied-to, so it is
echoed here instead, on its own axis, the same split entityPlacement makes for
a supersede's inherited placement.

derived.description:
Derived marks a PART_OF placement the tree infers rather than one stored as a
graph edge: a filing by `path:` tag, or an entry in the Unfiled bucket.

cluster_fqn.description:
ClusterFQN is the top-level section the node sits under, for grouping and
collapsing. Empty for the root and for estate objects, which bridge sections.
When set it always names another node of the SAME response, so a client can
title the group it is asked to draw; a cluster the response does not contain is
dropped rather than emitted as a bare fqn (see baseGraphBuilder.result).

count.description:
Count is the number of entries under a section (or the whole base, for the
root), counted the way the tree counts them.

generated.description:
Generated marks a section with no page of its own (a `path:` folder, or the
Unfiled bucket on an account that has no Unfiled node). There is nothing to
open for it.

node_type.description: NodeType is root, section, entry, estate, term, or account.

status.description:
Status is the leaf's real status (FL-31650, cw#453 gap #1) — set by
baseLeafNode, never by a section node (a section carries no
meaningful status of its own on the wire; the SPA's wireEntryRef only
ever reads this off a non-section child). See baseEntryStatus for what
values this can take and why "proposed"/"superseded" are part of the
type but structurally unreachable through this read today.

deferred.description:
Deferred holds the bulk_seed_ambiguity rows raised by this run. On an executed run
these are the PERSISTED rows, fully identified. On a dry run they are PREVIEWS of
the rows that would be created: item_type, status, reason, account_id and
proposed_payload are exact, while review_item_id, source_event_id and created_at
are minted at persist time and so carry no value here. Nothing else returns a
ReviewItem with unset identity fields.

On the wire that means the two ids are OMITTED from a preview row (they carry
omitempty for exactly this path), matching the generated optional TS type. The one
residue is created_at: time.Time has no useful zero-omission, so a preview stamps
it "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z". A consumer must therefore treat created_at on a dry-run
row as absent rather than parse it — `new Date(row.created_at)` yields a year-1
date, which is worse than an absent one because nothing downstream flags it.
Removing that last one needs a preview-specific type or *time.Time; both change
the contract and are scoped out of this ticket.

knowledge_scope_id.description:
ScopeID is required for the project, user, and session scopes (each names a
specific subject) and MAY be empty for account (defaults to the request-context
account) and flume_core (global, no id). See Validate.

proposed_target.description:
ProposedTarget is the attachment target the proposer named, as TEXT. Required to
approve (FR-27 "resolved attachment target"). It is deliberately neither of the
two things it resembles: not an :APPLIES_TO edge (attach needs a RESOLVED fqn,
and a proposer has not resolved anything), and not Applicability (which is prose
about WHEN the knowledge applies, not WHAT it attaches to). Resolution is the
curator's job on the manage surface before approval.

sensitivity.description:
Sensitivity is the proposer's PHI classification (none | phi_adjacent |
phi_bearing). Required to approve (FR-27 "sensitivity classification"); an
unclassified entity is not injectable (PHI policy §4).

supersedes_fqn.description:
SupersedesFQN is the predecessor a draft carries (FL-31264, spec-e4-wiki-edit-loop
Part 3 gap 2, CT8). It is accepted ONLY on a status=proposed create — a proposal
"lands as a supersede" but must not link + flip the predecessor until a curator
approves it (AD-3: a curator publishes; the predecessor stays active and readable
until then), so :supersede's proposed-status branch holds this on the review row
instead of calling Manager.Supersede. promoteProposal runs the actual link + flip
inside the SAME approve call the predecessor's status was frozen against
(Q1, decided 2026-09-15: one act, approval runs the supersede).

It is the literal wire name a context-workspace lane (FL-31295) is building
against tonight without seeing this code — do not rename it.

verification_interval.description:
VerificationInterval is the re-verification cadence (an ISO-8601 duration string
such as "P90D" — see knowledgestore.Duration), required to approve (FR-27
"verification interval").

It is accepted at PROPOSE time, which is a deviation worth stating: it is an
approver-shaped decision, and the natural home would be the approve request. But
the review-queue's approve is a bodyless POST by contract, so with no create-time
field a proposal could carry no interval by any route the SPA has, and every
promotion would block on missing evidence permanently. The approve route still
accepts an override, so the approver keeps the final say; this field is what
lets the proposal arrive with a defensible default already on it.

state.description:
State is the state found. After a POST wrote the item, State is the state
the write reached (present or absent) and Action names the write.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the scan hit its page budget. The report is then
a lower bound and an entry past the budget reads as missing.

entries_placed.description:
EntriesPlaced is the same count for every other active entry, filed
under Unfiled.

nodes_scanned.description:
NodesScanned is every :Knowledge node this run read while looking for
unplaced ones — reported so an operator can tell "scanned everything,
found nothing to move" from "the scan itself did nothing".

sections_placed.description:
SectionsPlaced is the count of pre-existing kind:ontology entries this
run found with no :PART_OF edge and filed under the root.

singletons_repaired.description:
SingletonsRepaired counts the fixed-fqn sections this run found present
but DRIFTED — non-active, or no longer kind:ontology — and restored. Zero
on a healthy account, and zero on every run after the first that repaired
one. Non-zero means something mutated a system section directly; the
`edited` audit events this run emitted carry hierarchy_repair=true.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the node scan hit its page budget
(maxListScanPages * listPageSize) with a full final page — meaning the
account has more :Knowledge vertices than one pass can read, and any
orphan past NodesScanned still carries no :PART_OF edge.

It matters more than an ordinary "there is more data" flag because this
scan is NOT resumable: `after` always restarts at "", EnsureHierarchy
takes no cursor, and so every subsequent run re-reads the same first
NodesScanned rows. An operator who reads a 200 with truncated=false as
"reconciled" would be right; one who reads truncated=true has to know
the tail is unreachable through this endpoint and needs the corpus
shrunk or a paged reconcile.

Reported rather than refused, unlike the edge-read ceiling below
(KnowledgeWriteLimitExceeded), because the two failures differ: a
truncated EDGE read makes the placements this pass DID write unsafe (a
node whose edges were cut from the tail looks unplaced and gets
double-filed), while a truncated NODE scan leaves every placement it
made correct and merely incomplete. Refusing would throw away real work;
reporting keeps it and still tells the truth. This mirrors
scanWikiNodes, which reports the identical condition as `truncated`
(wiki_export.go:683) rather than failing the export.

kinds.description: Kinds is one row per kind and status, sorted by kind then status.

nodesScanned.description: NodesScanned is every :Knowledge node this census read.

ontologyWithChildren.description:
OntologyWithChildren counts `ontology` entries that at least one
:Knowledge entry files under with a :PART_OF edge. Each is a section
that FL-31834 must rewrite to `area`. The hierarchy's root and Unfiled
singletons are left out of both ontology counts: every account that has
any knowledge has them, repairHierarchySingletons forces them back to
`ontology`, and counting them would report drift no POST can clear.

ontologyWithoutChildren.description:
OntologyWithoutChildren counts the other `ontology` entries, singletons
excluded.

outsideBuiltIn.description: OutsideBuiltIn counts entries whose kind is not built in.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the node scan hit its page budget or the edge
read hit its row ceiling. The counts are then a lower bound.

after.description:
After continues an "all" pass: only entries whose fqn sorts after it are
considered. Pass the previous proposal's next_after.

limit.description: Limit caps the entries considered. Zero or over the ceiling means the ceiling.

why.example: It describes a claim intake failure.

description.example: How claims reach the pipeline and what can fail on the way.

why.description: Why is the one-line reason for the area. Apply ignores it.
why.example: Six entries describe claim intake and no area covers it.

retitles.description:
Retitles and AreaMoves are optional on apply, so a client that predates them
sends a valid plan.

advice.description: Advice holds the merges, splits and links a curator carries out by hand.

considered.description: Considered is how many entries the proposer saw.

dropped.description:
Dropped counts plan lines the validator removed because they named nothing real
or gave no reason.

next_after.description: NextAfter is the After value for the next "all" pass, "" when none remain.

remaining.description:
Remaining is how many matching entries the proposal did not cover because of the
limit. Run the step again after applying to take the next pass.

unassigned.description:
Unassigned lists the considered entries the plan leaves where they are. A model
that gives no filing for an entry, or a filing the validator drops, ends up here.

area_fqn.description:
AreaFQN is the area the entry is filed under: an active area
(kind:ontology) entry the caller can read. Empty files a published entry
under Unfiled and leaves a proposal for the approver to place.

sensitivity.description:
Sensitivity is the saver's PHI classification (none | phi_adjacent |
phi_bearing). It is written on the entry in both outcomes.

verification_interval.description: VerificationInterval is the re-verification cadence, such as "P90D".

area_fqn.description:
AreaFQN is the area the entry is filed under now (published), or the area
the approval files it under (proposed). Empty when the save named no area,
or when a published entry could not be filed under it and went to Unfiled.

entity.description: Entity is the entry the save wrote: active when published, proposed otherwise.

outcome.description: Outcome is publish or propose. DecideKnowledgeWrite decided it.

confidence.description:
Confidence is presence-aware: nil means "no confidence supplied" (the property
is omitted at persistence), while a non-nil pointer persists its value —
including a legal 0.0 — so "zero confidence" and "unset" round-trip distinctly
instead of collapsing to the same stored state.

inherited.description:
Inherited marks an edge the SERVER wrote on a curator's behalf rather than one
a curator's own :attach call created — today only the supersede-approval copy
(FL-31324, knowledgemanager.copyPredecessorPlacement). It is persisted as the
EdgePropInherited property so the distinction survives the write, which is what
the retry path needs: that copy has no cross-edge transaction (kernel.go:264),
so a mid-loop failure leaves some edges committed, and without this marker the
retry reads the server's own partial write back as the curator's placement and
suppresses the rest of the axis. Omitted at persistence when false, so a
curator's attach is unmarked and stays theirs.

description.example: Rows written before 2021-03 have a null paid_amt.

title.example: paid_amt is null before the 2021 migration

freshness.description: Freshness is the verification/recency band (see FreshnessBand).

source.description: Source is the provenance gradient label (e.g. "curator", "scan", "inferred").

graph.description:
Graph names the graph the row came from: GraphAccount or GraphFlume. context-db
sets it on a merged search only; an empty value means the account graph.

scope.description:
Scope is the vertex's promoted scope column, when context-db returns it.
The manager reads it to drop a workspace-scoped :Artifact hit (FL-32099),
whose scope is not in Properties.

sensitivityCeiling.description:
SensitivityCeiling is the most restrictive PHI classification this user
may see (FL-31456). Read-only here — set only via
PUT /api/v1/users/{id}/sensitivity-ceiling (SystemAdmin only).

id.description:
ID is the caller's numeric platform user id, the key workspace members
are listed under. It lives here and not on User, which other responses
share.

sensitivityCeiling.description:
SensitivityCeiling is the most restrictive PHI classification this user
may see (FL-31456). Read-only here — set only via
PUT /api/v1/users/{id}/sensitivity-ceiling (SystemAdmin only).

active.description: pointer so we can distinguish between false and not set

connectionId.description:
A pointer so an absent field ("required") is told apart from a zero or
negative one ("must be a positive integer").

conversationId.description:
ConversationID is the conversation the artifact came from, when the
caller named one. Informational: it grants nothing.

conversationOpenable.description:
ConversationOpenable is true when the caller can open the chat named
by conversationId.

conversationTitle.description:
ConversationTitle is the chat's title, set only when
ConversationOpenable is true.

instructions.description:
Instructions replaces the project's instructions for the assistant
(FL-31666); "" clears them. At most 8,000 characters.

workspaceOnly.description:
WorkspaceOnly is true when the connection answers only inside the
workspaces it is attached to (FL-31882), so the page can say so.

addTime.description:
AddTime is always nil today — not because the data does not exist, but
because it is not exposed on the wire this package reads. context-db's
_authz_tuples dataset carries written_at/written_by on every row
(crates/context-catalog/src/authz/tuples.rs's own Arrow schema), but
TupleWire — what /authz/tuples/query actually returns
(crates/context-server/src/authz_handlers.rs) — is Subject/Relation/
Object/ExpiresAt and nothing else. AuthzTuple (knowledgestore package)
mirrors that wire exactly, which is why this package can go no further.
FL-31490 is the read-side fix on context-db's end; once it lands this
field stops being permanently nil. Nil here follows Counts' own idiom
in this file until then: nil means "not yet available," never a
fabricated zero a client could mistake for "just now."

committed.description:
Committed is true from AddMember, false from PreviewAddMember — the
same shape either way. Neither the REST facade's addMemberRequest.
ValidateOnly nor the MCP tool's validate_only argument is safe to trust
as the caller's only signal: a caller who mistypes either one gets the
other branch silently — a preview that commits, or a commit reported
back byte-identical to a preview, with nothing in the response saying
which happened. This field is what lets a caller verify the outcome
from the answer itself rather than trusting the request it sent.

counts.description:
Counts, DataSources, NoDirectGrant, DataSourcesAvailable and Committed
are the D4 disclosure — set only by AddMember/PreviewAddMember, nil/
omitted from every other Member this package returns. See
computeDisclosure.

dataSources.description:
DataSources names the project's data sources; NoDirectGrant lists, of
those, the ones the new member has no direct grant on today — the
warning Casey asked for. Never a conversation title; see the package
doc.

dataSourcesAvailable.description:
DataSourcesAvailable is false while project-scoped data connections
remain unbuilt (see the package doc) — DataSources and NoDirectGrant
are always empty in that state, and a caller must read the state from
this field, not from the slices being empty, which would also be the
shape of "no data sources, checked, none found." A *bool, not bool: nil
means "not applicable to this Member" (every non-disclosure caller),
false means "computed, and there are none" (the disclosure callers).

displayName.description:
DisplayName is resolved via UserLookup, the same lookup AddMember
already uses for its tenancy check. Empty when resolution fails — a
missing name must never block listing the membership itself.

standing.description:
Standing is "approver", "curator" or "member" — the highest of the
DIRECT grants (approver_grant, curator_grant, member) this subject
holds on THIS project, per QueryTuples filtered by object alone.
Deliberately not the full computed reader/approver/curator relation:
that can also be true through account-wide inheritance (`approver from
parent`), which this endpoint would need a Check call per member per
relation to see, and a project's member LIST is not the place to pay
for that. A bare member with neither grant reads "member".

callerIsOwner.description:
CallerIsOwner is true when the caller created the project (FL-31698).
Set by GetProject and CreateProject only. The workspace has no numeric
user id of its own, so this is how it knows whether to offer the role
control. It is a display hint: ChangeMemberRole still checks.

instructions.description:
Instructions is the project's standing guidance for the assistant
(FL-31666), carried into every chat turn in the project (FL-31667).
Readers read it; approvers edit it, which covers every curator (D12).
See instructions.go and instructions_entry.go.

instructionsUpdatedBy.description:
InstructionsUpdatedBy is the numeric platform user id of the last
editor.

instructionsVersion.description:
InstructionsVersion counts changes to Instructions; 0 means they have
never been set.

conversationId.description:
ConversationID is the conversation the artifact came from, when the
caller named one. Informational: it grants nothing.

callerCanEdit.description:
CallerCanEdit is true when the caller may change the instructions:
approver on the workspace, which every curator is (D12). The app shows
Edit only then. The write path makes its own check; this flag grants
nothing.

entry.description:
Entry is RenderInstructionsEntry for the current version: the exact text
a workspace chat's history must hold. Empty when the version is 0.

instructionsUpdatedBy.description:
InstructionsUpdatedBy is the numeric platform user id of the last
editor.

archiveTime.description:
ArchiveTime is nil for an active project — never a zero time, which a
client would have to know to special-case.

conversationCount.description:
ConversationCount is nil until FL-31456 (project-scoped conversation
counting) exists — conversations carry no project_id yet (FL-31451).
Same "not yet available" idiom as Counts below: nil, never a
fabricated zero.

lastActivityTime.description:
LastActivityTime is the later of the vertex's last_activity_at (create,
rename, describe, archive) and the workspace_activity row (FL-32030):
a chat joining, changing or leaving, a turn landing, an artifact,
member or data-source change. Every change moves it; there is no
throttle. It orders the sidebar. For which part changed, read
GET /workspaces/{id}/activity.

memberCount.description:
MemberCount is real, computed per row as the number of distinct users
holding a direct `member` tuple (one extra QueryTuples call per row — the same N+1
shape this method already accepts for GetNode per row).
